## Parser subsystem overview

Top-level entry: `Parser` class holds a `TreeBuilder` (either `HtmlTreeBuilder` or `XmlTreeBuilder`), plus settings/errors/tagset. `Parser.parseInput` just locks and delegates to `treeBuilder.parse(...)` (Parser.java:88-95). Static factories `htmlParser()`/`xmlParser()` pick tree builder impl (Parser.java:369-380).

### TreeBuilder (base, abstract)
`TreeBuilder` (abstract) owns the shared plumbing: `CharacterReader reader`, `Tokeniser tokeniser`, `Document doc`, stack of open `Element`s, current token, settings, tagset (TreeBuilder.java:22-32). Init sets up reader/tokeniser/doc per parse (TreeBuilder.java:41-62). Main loop: `runParser()` calls `stepParser()` repeatedly until EOF is fully drained; each step pulls one `Token` from tokeniser (`tokeniser.read()`), stores as `currentToken`, and calls abstract `process(token)` (TreeBuilder.java:105-130). `process(Token)` is abstract — each concrete tree builder implements its own dispatch (TreeBuilder.java:130). Base class also provides shared stack ops (`push`/`pop`), depth-limit enforcement (`enforceStackDepthLimit`, TreeBuilder.java:182-189), default namespace (`NamespaceHtml`, TreeBuilder.java:273-275) and default tagset (`TagSet.Html()`, TreeBuilder.java:277-279), both overridden by XML side.

### Tokeniser (lexer / low-level state machine)
`Tokeniser` reads chars off `CharacterReader` and turns them into `Token`s, driven by a `TokeniserState state` field (Tokeniser.java:34-37). `read()` loops `state.read(this, reader)` until a token is emitted (Tokeniser.java:64-77). Knows `syntax` (html vs xml) captured at construction from whether tree builder is `XmlTreeBuilder` (Tokeniser.java:56). Produces token types: Doctype, StartTag, EndTag, Comment, Character, XmlDecl, EOF (Token.java:620-626).

`TokeniserState` is a big enum, one state per method `read(Tokeniser,CharacterReader)`, implementing HTML5 tokenizer states — Data, TagOpen, RCDATA/rawtext/scriptdata variants, attribute states, comment/doctype states, plus XML-specific `MarkupProcessingOpen` (PI) and `CdataSection` (TokeniserState.java:11-1677, listing ~60 states e.g. TokeniserState.java:12,100,151,927,940,965,1677). Transition to next state via `t.transition(...)`/`t.advanceTransition(...)` (Tokeniser.java:118-129). `TagOpen` state branches on `t.syntax == xml` to go to `MarkupProcessingOpen` for `<?`, else treats it as bogus comment for HTML (TokeniserState.java:110-116).

### Tree builder state machine (parser proper)
`HtmlTreeBuilder extends TreeBuilder` implements `process(Token)` by dispatching to a **second** state machine, `HtmlTreeBuilderState` — an enum of HTML5 "insertion modes" (Initial, BeforeHtml, BeforeHead, InHead, InBody, Text, InTable, ... AfterAfterFrameset, ForeignContent — ~23 states, HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:25-1746). Each state implements `process(Token t, HtmlTreeBuilder tb)` (abstract at HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:1853) mutating the open-element stack/doc and possibly calling `tb.transition(...)` to move to another insertion mode (example: `Initial` state builds doctype then `tb.transition(BeforeHtml)`, HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:25-50).

`HtmlTreeBuilder.process` first checks a "noscript island" special-case (HtmlTreeBuilder.java:152-154), then decides whether to use the current insertion-mode state or divert to the special `ForeignContent` state via `useCurrentOrForeignInsert(token)` (HtmlTreeBuilder.java:155-156). That helper implements the HTML5 "adjusted current node" foreign-content rules (MathML text integration points, HTML integration points, empty stack, EOF) per spec (HtmlTreeBuilder.java:233-270), and `ForeignContent` state itself implements the spec's in-foreign-content algorithm, occasionally falling back to `processAsHtml` (HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:1746-1836).

There's a feedback loop between the two state machines: tree-builder states, on seeing tags like `title`, `script`, `style`, `textarea`, or custom raw/rcdata tags (via `Tag.textState()`, Tag.java:344), push the tokeniser into a different lexing mode (e.g. `ScriptData`, `Rawtext`) so raw markup content isn't tokenised as tags — done both when entering head (HtmlTreeBuilder.java:113-115), in `InHead`/`InBody` states (HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:136-145,593-595), and even inside `ForeignContent` for e.g. embedded SVG `script` (HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:1783-1789).

### XmlTreeBuilder — how it differs
`XmlTreeBuilder extends TreeBuilder` too, but its `process(Token)` is a single flat `switch` on token type — StartTag → `insertElementFor`, EndTag → `popStackToClose`, Comment/Character/Doctype/XmlDecl → direct leaf-node inserts (XmlTreeBuilder.java:114-144). There is **no** analogous "insertion-mode" enum for XML: no `HtmlTreeBuilderState`-style state machine, no auto-generated implicit elements, no foster-parenting/foreign-content algorithm, no formatting-element reconstruction — XML trusts the input structure directly.

Concrete structural differences baked into the two TreeBuilder subclasses:
- Default settings: HTML default settings vs XML `ParseSettings.preserveCase` (case-preserving) (HtmlTreeBuilder.java:58-60 vs XmlTreeBuilder.java:42-44).
